Lamu coastal hazard and exposure

Who and what sits inside, or close to, the county's projected sea-level-rise zone, and how hot has the sea been? The zone is mostly mangrove and tidal flats, so the exposure of people and buildings is concentrated in a few places.

Marine heat stress, peak

Click the map for the distance to the zone, the population of the cell and the ward. The slider widens the zone by a distance, a way to test how sensitive the numbers are to where the boundary falls; it is not a modelled flood. Turn layers on and off in the panel.

Spatial and data checks run
Sea-level-rise zone: validity, parts, area (UTM) vs attribute Shape_Areavalid=True, 17887 parts, 293.3 km² vs 295.6 km² in Web Mercator (+0.8%)

People inside the zone, whole county / share3527 / 2.0%
Distance-to-zone raster uses the same grid as the population overlaybounds differ by 0.000000 degrees
Distance overlay vs exact vector distance at 4,000 random population cells within 2.8 kmmedian absolute difference 31 m, 90% within 78 m (raster is 100 m, 20 m steps, thin parts counted)
Zone outline drawn on the map: simplified to 60 m, parts under 1 ha dropped (the distance layer keeps all parts)1318 of 17887 parts kept, area 86.5% of the original
Cultural sites: recorded elevation vs distance to the zone58 sites with elevation; median elevation 20 m; 10 within 1 km of the zone, their median elevation 7 m vs 22 m for the rest
What the layer isOnly 26 of the layer's 293 km² overlap the ward land outlines. Inside the study area, 3,508 of its 4,695 ha are flooded vegetation, 591 ha trees, 271 ha bare ground and 6 ha built-up (land cover 2026), and 57% of the study-area mangrove lies inside it. It marks mangrove and tidal ground far more than settled land.
Method range for peopleCounting each 5-ha cell by its centre puts 3,527 people inside the zone; weighting by the overlapping part of each cell gives 4,752.
Sensitivity to thin parts16,437 of the zone's 17,887 parts are under 1 ha. They barely change the count inside the zone but drive the proximity figures: within 500 m, people fall from 64,150 to 32,766 and buildings from 7,748 to 2,679 if they are ignored. Both are shown.
Method changeWalking distances to leave the zone now use fast marching (see dashboard 4); people who can walk out of the zone within 0.5 km rose from 890 to 2,495, and within 1 km stays at 3,521 of 3,527.
Not in the dataNo elevation model, no scenario or height for the layer, no flood depth, and the village flood-prone field is blank, so this is an exposure screen by distance and not a flood model.
Not testable offlineAlignment against live basemap tiles. Overlays use the same Web Mercator grid as the tiles; registration against the source rasters is tested above.

The sea-level-rise layer is the county database layer named Projected_Sea_Level_Rise_2025 (one multipart polygon, 293 km²); its scenario, height and method are not documented in the data. Only 26 km² of it overlaps the ward land outlines; inside the study area three-quarters is flooded vegetation (mangrove and tidal flats) and 6 ha is built-up. Recorded elevations of cultural sites near it are lower (median 7 m, against 22 m elsewhere), which supports it marking low-lying ground, but there is no elevation model in the data to test or extend it. People are counted by cell centre (3,527 inside the zone); counting the part of each 5-hectare cell that overlaps gives 4,752, so read exposure as a range. The zone also has 16,437 parts under 1 ha along creeks; they drive the proximity numbers, so ignoring them roughly halves the count within 500 m (people 64,150 to 32,766, buildings 7,748 to 2,679) while the count inside barely moves (3,527 to 3,322). Buildings are Open Buildings footprints and cover the study area only; built-up land is smoothed over three years. Walking distances assume land routes only, no boats. The village layer's flood-prone field is empty and four villages carry an evacuation flag, so no assessment of evacuation capacity is possible. Heat stress is an estimate from satellite sea-surface temperature near the port (see dashboard 3). Basemaps © OpenStreetMap contributors, CARTO, Esri, OpenTopoMap, Mapbox.
